prize_parts.citation: For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage, through engineered nucleobase deaminases guided to a chosen site
For the conception and demonstration of targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional PROTAC molecules that recruit the ubiquitin-proteasome system

statement.case_for: I keep the same configuration after the full first round: base editing credited to Liu, and PROTAC-based targeted protein degradation credited to Crews and Deshaies. The test I apply is whether a designed molecular principle changed what researchers and clinicians can do. Base editors do that by making a deaminase reaction programmable at one base pair without a double-strand break or donor template. They have been reproduced in very many laboratories and are in patients. PROTACs do it by turning a binder into a remover and reaching proteins that have no active site to inhibit. The ternary-complex mechanism is quantifiable, and the 2001 Sakamoto-Kim-Crews-Deshaies paper is a clean founding concept. The round-1 exchange sharpened two points for me. First, the chair asked which step is the discovery. For base editing it is the evolved, DNA-acting deaminase fused to a nickase-guided protein, which is the Liu programme and not the old deamination chemistry. For degradation it is the rational, heterobifunctional recruitment of an E3 ligase, which is chemical design applied to a biological pathway. Second, four of us independently arrived at the same three-person union, which tells me the arithmetic is workable, but I do not treat that count as evidence of merit. I weigh the science, and on the science these two parts are the most generative on the shortlist.
statement.case_against: The cost of this configuration is real and I will not hide it. Liu alone leaves out Komor and Gaudelli, who wrote the two decisive base-editor papers, and Gaudelli's evolution of an adenine deaminase acting on DNA is the clearest new chemistry in the field. Crews and Deshaies leave out Handa and Ito, whose cereblon work underlies the molecular-glue lineage, and Ciulli and Gray. On timing, base editing sits near the 2020 genome-editing prize, and no PROTAC is yet an approved drug, so the clinical proof on that part is incomplete and I would rest its citation on the concept and mechanism, not on therapies. A reasonable colleague can also say that a two-part prize in chemical biology shares its theme only loosely. If the committee judges the Liu-only credit indefensible, I would take B024 as a single part with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli before I would drop either of those three names to protect a second part.

responses.point: Chabes proposes a single-part base-editing prize for Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, argues adenine base editing is the strongest evidence of real chemistry because TadA had to be evolved to act on DNA, and rejects Nishida and Kondo as less general.
responses.response: I agree with his chemical argument and it is the reason I will not call Komor and Gaudelli mere trainees. Where I still differ is allocation. With the three-person cap, his trio takes every seat on one part and leaves no room for degradation, which I judge to be the second strongest achievement. I would rather put the evolved-deaminase contribution into the citation text and credit Liu, whose programme produced both editor classes, than split the prize into a trainee-inclusive single part. I do concede that if the committee finds Liu-only untenable, his version is my fallback. On Target-AID, I still read Nishida and Kondo as a parallel architecture that did not generalise as the Liu editors did, but I cannot verify the priority record here and agree the chair should have it checked before the vote.

responses.point: Somfai holds B003 first with B024 as Liu alone, and argues that the new chemistry in base editing is largely protein engineering and directed evolution on top of the 2020 CRISPR prize, which makes a mixed prize look thematically loose.
responses.response: His objection is the most serious one against my B024 part, and I take it seriously. My answer is that the chemical step is a nucleobase deamination carried out by enzymes evolved to act on DNA and tied to a nickase, so the outcome is a defined, single-base chemical conversion with no strand break, which Cas9 cutting does not provide. That is why I put the evolved deaminase and the break-free outcome, and not the CRISPR platform, in the citation. I am less persuaded that B003 is stronger. Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is mature and cleanly attributed, but the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the Kosugi precursor make it incremental in a way base editing is not, and I do not see it adding to my configuration in the way degradation does.

responses.point: Brzezinski supports the same two parts, argues PROTACs are chemistry because the ternary-complex mechanism is quantitative, and names the Handa and Ito cereblon lineage as the main gap in the credit.
responses.response: I agree that induced proximity is molecular design and measurable ternary-complex energetics, and that answers the chemistry-versus-biology objection better than my own round-1 wording did. On Handa and Ito, I think we should keep the two histories separate. The cereblon molecular-glue lineage is a drug-discovery story built around serendipity and later mechanism, while the 2001 PROTAC is a deliberately designed bifunctional molecule. Merging them in one citation would blur both, and three seats cannot carry both without breaking the cap, so I keep Crews and Deshaies and word the citation on heterobifunctional recruitment.

responses.point: Aqvist offered to shift the degradation part from Crews and Deshaies to Handa if the committee decides the molecular-glue lineage is the mature core, and would anchor the citation on the 2001 concept.
responses.response: I do not think the evidence supports moving to Handa. Cereblon explains how thalidomide-class drugs act, which is a mechanism discovery, while the Crews-Deshaies concept created a general design rule that any laboratory can use with a new ligand. That generality is what changes practice. I do accept his point that the absence of an approved PROTAC drug weakens any argument based on therapies, so I agree the citation should rest on concept and mechanism, and I would be uneasy if the committee leaned on clinical numbers.

responses.point: Sparr proposes lipid nanoparticles alone (Cullis, Hope, Madden) on a pKa-tuned charge and non-bilayer phase-behaviour argument, and herself flags the 2023 Medicine prize overlap and her proximity to the field.
responses.response: I find her physical-chemical case the strongest case for a delivery prize and I ranked B013 third for the same reason. I also respect her for stating her proximity openly. My hesitation stays attribution, since the trio omits MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer, and the priority split between the ionizable lipid and the formulation process is, as she says, contested. That is why B013 stays my first alternative and not part of my configuration.

uncertainties: Whether the Kondo and Nishida Target-AID priority record changes who can be credited for base editing or only how the citation is worded; I cannot verify the dates here.
Whether the committee accepts Liu alone for B024, or finds that leaving out Komor and Gaudelli makes the citation untenable.
Whether the 2001 Crews-Deshaies concept is the right anchor for degradation or the Handa and Ito cereblon lineage is the mature core.
Whether base editing reads as a distinct chemical advance or as a follow-on to the 2020 genome-editing prize.
Whether pairing base editing with degradation reads as a coherent chemical-biology prize or only a loosely shared theme.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name is apparent. My postdoc mentors (Molly Stevens, Freddy Boey) and Linkoping colleagues are not credited on the shortlist, and I have no collaboration with Liu, Crews, Deshaies or the other candidates. I note only overlapping research interests with Emma Sparr in self-assembly and peptide systems, and my work in peptide-nanoparticle biosensing is near but not part of B013 or any other part of my configuration. No change from round 1.
